races.name: Industry Leading In-Play Markets At Unibet Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Big Bear Hug
runners_data.note: Out-and-out hold-up specialist for Jim Boyle, returning after a 50-day absence which is a concern; all recent sim-going efforts show no wins and no places in 15 attempts, making the Standard to Slow surface a significant question mark at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Big Bear Hug capped a mixed sequence with a third last time and is proven at today's trip and going, form that leads these ratings. She's yet to win in this run and carries 140lb from draw three, but the improved effort hints she's finding form now.

runners_data.name: Valentine Boy
runners_data.note: Won over 1m on Standard AW going and has placed three times in 11 similar-going runs — the step up to 1m3f is a new ask for this four-year-old; headgear (hood) may help settle, and Jude Fernandes claiming 3lbs is a meaningful weight swing in a tight field.
runners_data.comment: Valentine Boy won three starts back but has since dipped, with a fourth and last time's eighth following that success, though today's going is already proven for him. A brisk 18-day turnaround and first-time hood offer hope of a bounce, with an unproven trip and that recent form the concerns.

runners_data.name: Sarangpur
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at Goodwood over 1m2-1m3f put this four-year-old in the best recent form in the race; naturally a deep hold-up horse pushed forward on the map by redistribution, so discount any expectation of it racing prominently — it will come from off the pace regardless of its charted position.
runners_data.comment: Sarangpur arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and is fresh from just a seven-day break, form that makes him hard to ignore. He already has today's trip in the book, though today's going looks new to him, and a modest speed figure is the one query on paper.

runners_data.name: Sonnerie Power
runners_data.note: A strikingly consistent AW performer with 15 from 15 runs on Standard going in its history and a win over 11f on Standard recently; though its true style is to close from the rear rather than race mid-division as charted here, its all-weather record makes it one of the most course-condition-reliable horses in this field.
runners_data.comment: Sonnerie Power bounced back with a clear second last time, having found only modest form in between since a win earlier in this sequence, though today's trip and going are already proven for him. His speed figure stands out among these dangers, with the earlier dip the only note of caution.

runners_data.name: Distinction
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has shown only two placed runs in 15 similar-going attempts, which is a concern; at eight years old this gelding carries experience but its recent form string (056836) doesn't inspire confidence, and while it is a genuine hold-up type rather than the midfield runner the map suggests, the going stats are not encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Distinction has been competitive without landing a win in his last six starts, with a third his best effort among mostly midfield finishes, and he is proven at today's trip and going. First-time visor could sharpen him, though the pattern of finishes leaves him short of a leading claim.

runners_data.name: Brodie's Boy
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's yard is in form (T14: 13/57) and Brodie's Boy has four places from 15 similar-going runs showing consistency without a win; a natural closer rather than a midfield runner despite its charted position, and Charlie Tucker's 5lb claim is a helpful weight allowance if the race becomes a sprint finish.
runners_data.comment: Brodie's Boy remains without a win in his last six starts, with a third his best effort amid modest finishes, though he is proven at today's trip and going. His speed figure is notably higher than his rating suggests, and a brisk 15-day turnaround keeps him fresh for this puzzle.

runners_data.name: Maywedance
runners_data.note: Won over 1m3f on Standard AW going and carries the lowest weight at 128lbs — John O'Shea's yard is quiet (T14: 0/7) but the horse's distance-proven AW record and placed run over 1m3f last time out make it interesting; a true hold-up runner in reality, its light weight could be the differentiator if this becomes an extreme late-sprint.
runners_data.comment: Maywedance ended a mixed sequence with a third last time out, having won earlier in this run of starts, and she is already proven at today's trip and going. First-time cheekpieces add a slight unknown, but she rates bottom of this field and has plenty of laboured efforts to overcome.

races.paceDynamic: This is a field of seven confirmed hold-up horses with no genuine front-runner or prominent racer in the field, meaning no horse has any natural incentive to make the pace and the race is almost certain to crawl before erupting into a sprint-finish from the home turn. The Standard to Slow surface at Kempton AW will compound this dynamic, as horses will be reluctant to expend energy early and the pack will bunch tightly through the early and middle stages. Sarangpur, Sonnerie Power, Distinction, Brodie's Boy and Maywedance are all true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map purely because there are more closers than the chart can accommodate at the rear — none of them will naturally be pressing forward. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the horse who can produce the sharpest late burst from the widest pool of closers, with finishing kick and recent course-and-distance form at this Kempton configuration the decisive factors; horses proven over this 1m3f AW trip with a strong closing pattern carry the structural edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish, Closers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls throughout and the race detonates into a mass sprint off the home turn with no horse having gone clear early.
scenarios.body: With no pace-setter, the entire field arrives at the 2f marker in a cluster and it becomes a pure test of late acceleration on a Standard to Slow surface; horses with proven finishing speed over this Kempton trip and recent winning form at the distance have the structural advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Recent Form Holds Sway
scenarios.trigger: If the best-performed runners over this trip and this going on AW produce a finish that mirrors their recent form profiles.
scenarios.body: Sarangpur's back-to-back wins at Goodwood over 1m2f-1m3f show a horse in peak form, and Sonnerie Power's consistent Standard-going AW record gives it strong claims in this type of race; the Standard to Slow surface suits horses with proven AW credentials over the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Maywedance Exploits Low Weight
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly suicidal-slow and the race becomes an extreme test of finishing stamina where the lightest-weighted runners with proven distance form hold a decisive physical advantage.
scenarios.body: Maywedance carries the lowest weight at 128lbs, has won over 1m3f on Standard AW going and was placed over this exact trip at Goodwood last time; the combination of light weight, distance-proven form and a horse in reasonable recent form could prove decisive in an extreme crawl-then-sprint.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Veteran Experience Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops an unpredictable rhythm and accumulated course and race experience outweighs raw form figures, favouring older horses who have handled this shape before.
scenarios.body: Distinction (age 8) and Big Bear Hug (age 7) have both navigated enough races of this type to position professionally and avoid interference in a bunched finish; Sonnerie Power's 15-from-15 runs on Standard going underlines a veteran who rarely runs a bad race in these conditions.

watchPoints.text: With all seven runners being hold-up horses, watch for a crawl of extreme proportions in the early stages — any horse drawn or ridden to find a forward position even marginally could gain a decisive positional advantage from the home turn.

Sarangpur is the most in-form horse in the race but runs its last two wins at Goodwood turf — monitor whether it handles the Kempton AW surface on first contact, as a surface switch can catch even in-form horses cold.

Sonnerie Power's T14 strike rate (7/12) for David Killahena & Graeme McPherson is the highest trainer form figure in the race — the stable is firing and this horse's Standard-going AW reliability makes it dangerous if overlooked in the market.

Valentine Boy's headgear (hood) is noted — horses wearing hoods for the first time or returning to them after a break can show unpredictable early behaviour in a slow-run race and may unsettle the pack rhythm if it pulls or idles early.

Watch the weight spread: Big Bear Hug (140lbs) concedes 12lbs to Maywedance (128lbs) — in a race decided by a sprint finish off a slow pace, that weight differential over 1m3f on a slow surface is a non-trivial physical factor.

races.name: Unibet/British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Unibet/EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Alshera
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race, handled Standard AW going on her only start (won 1m2f), the Gosden yard are 6/48 over the past 14 days, 246 days off but clearly trained for this, and her ability to dictate unchallenged is the central tactical fact of this race.

runners_data.name: Crack Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Last ran just 10 days ago (11th and 12th in her two AW starts) and carries a fades-in-finish flag; her natural home is at the back of the field, but the overcrowded hold-up group means she will be pushed to midfield — a position that does not naturally suit her, compounding already modest form.

runners_data.name: Skittish
runners_data.note: Blinkered hold-up type returning after a 205-day jumps break, with all her turf form on Good or Soft; this Standard To Slow AW surface and the 1m3f trip are untested combinations for her and represent a significant unknown.

runners_data.name: Stopherandgo
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with all her form on Good or Soft turf at much longer distances (up to 25f); the drop to 1m3f on AW is a sharp change of context, and while she may push forward, her profile suggests this race is not made for her.

runners_data.name: Tide Lines
runners_data.note: Ran a respectable fourth over 1m last time (Good), is held up by Charlie Johnston and represents one of the more credible hold-up challengers if a run materialises through the home straight on the AW rail.

runners_data.name: Baba Ganoush
runners_data.note: Unraced debutante for Hughie Morrison with style unknown; Morrison has two winners from 11 runners over the past fortnight, and three-year-old unexposed types at Kempton can surprise, but she is a complete unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Blue Hill
runners_data.note: Finished fifth on debut over 1m on Good turf, style unmapped; the step to 1m3f AW is a significant ask on just one run and the form benchmark from that maiden is modest.

runners_data.name: Cracking Beauty
runners_data.note: Two-year-old whose natural style is hold-up but who has been pushed to midfield on the map due to traffic; her solitary start ended in an 11th-place finish, fades-in-finish flag is noted, and a 230-day absence adds considerable uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Kashooda
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Andrew Balding (7/57 in 14 days), finished third on her only AW start over 1m on Standard, and the step to 1m3f could unlock more; she is a lightly raced three-year-old whose ceiling is genuinely unknown and she fits the prominent-tracker profile well.

runners_data.name: Make A Splash
runners_data.note: Finished ninth over 1m6f on Good last time and carries a fades-in-finish flag; naturally a hold-up horse pushed to midfield by the overcrowded rear, meaning she will not be in her comfort zone and her most recent poor form offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Marianita
runners_data.note: Fourth on debut over 1m2f on Good for Ralph Beckett, style unknown but mapped mid-division; Beckett sends lightly raced fillies out to Kempton AW with intent and this horse's unexposed status means her handicapping ceiling could be considerably higher than one run suggests.

runners_data.name: Salve Allegra
runners_data.note: Ran seventh over 1m3f on Standard AW last time for Alan King, wears a hood, and has demonstrated she stays the trip on this exact surface and going; hold-up style is her natural game but the hood and AW course familiarity are points in her favour if she can find a clean run.

runners_data.name: Bintwafaa
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner; natural hold-up type on AW who was redistributed to midfield, so her absence does not materially alter the pace map — the overcrowding at the rear is still a feature with the remaining hold-up horses.

races.paceDynamic: Alshera is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, with just one rival (the gelding Stopherandgo) showing any inclination to race prominently, she can dictate an uncontested, measured gallop from the front on what is Standard To Slow ground — conditions that reward relaxed, economical racing. The bulk of the field is composed of true hold-up types (Crack Of Thunder, Make A Splash, Cracking Beauty, Bintwafaa) who have been redistributed to midfield on the map purely because the rear of the race is overcrowded, meaning they will not be running their natural race and their finishing kicks may be blunted by traffic and positional compromise. With Alshera able to control tempo and quicken on her own terms, this race shape heavily favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace in second or third, conserving energy before delivering a sustained late run — the classic Kempton AW profile of a horse that sits within two lengths of the leader before the home straight and stays on strongly. The field holds considerably more genuine hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear; of those, Crack Of Thunder, Make A Splash and Cracking Beauty are the most likely to attempt to claim a midfield berth, but their style-fit concerns mean their winning prospects in this shape are materially discounted.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alshera Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Alshera dictates an uncontested, even-tempo gallop and the hold-up horses are caught in traffic through the home straight.
scenarios.body: Alshera sets a sustainable pace into the final bend, giving her rider a controlled lead heading into the straight, and any horse travelling prominently just behind her inherits the cleanest ground and the best platform to challenge; horses forced widest from the rear in a slow-building pace simply arrive too late on a track that does not reward last-to-first runs when the fractions are not truly searching.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling second or third on the rail tracks Alshera through the final bend and produces a decisive move at the two-furlong marker.
scenarios.body: The unfussy gallop suits a horse with a prominent or mid-division style that has been travelling within itself, allowing a smooth transition into a finishing effort without having to cover excess ground; Kashooda and Marianita, both lightly raced three-year-olds with unknown ceilings, fit this profile best if their ability is above what their current form suggests.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and a gap opens on the inside or widest wide, allowing a genuine hold-up type a clear late run.
scenarios.body: This is conditional on Alshera tying up or the front runners stopping, which is unlikely given the steady fractions anticipated; Tide Lines and Skittish are the hold-up runners with the most credible profiles on distance and going, but all redistributed types face the compound risk of poor positioning and a pace that does not truly set them up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Rank Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the slow ground slows the pace further, the field bunches and the race becomes a sprint from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Alshera's early position becomes decisive because a sprint-finish in a bunched field rewards whoever is shortest to the line without cover; however, this scenario also benefits unknown quantities like Baba Ganoush and Blue Hill who have no form baggage and could outrun their inexperience in a muddling finish.

watchPoints.text: Alshera's complete control of fractions is the race's pivot — watch whether any rival attempts to push forward off the stalls and pressure her early, as even modest competition for the lead would transform the race shape and open it up for the hold-up group.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Crack Of Thunder, Make A Splash, Cracking Beauty) will converge in midfield during the first half-mile — watch for early crowding and bumping that could compromise multiple runners' races before they reach the home straight.

Kashooda's draw and early manoeuvring by Oisin Murphy in the first furlong is worth noting — if Murphy slots her into a prominent position quickly, she becomes a material factor in what is otherwise a race with thin prominent-running depth.

Standard To Slow ground has been recorded for this race all evening at Kempton; watch the pace clock through the first six furlongs — if the early splits are unusually slow, the race becomes a sprint-finish that distorts all pacemaking advantages and renders hold-up form irrelevant.

Baba Ganoush and Marianita are both debutante or near-debutante three-year-olds for handlers (Morrison, Beckett) who place horses with intent — watch their pre-race market moves as a signal of how seriously these yards fancy their chances on debut.

races.name: Unibet More Extra Place Races Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Caprelo
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner for Hughie Morrison with Tom Marquand aboard; has strong form on Standard going (3W5P at that condition) and recent winning form at this trip, though 47 days off the track and a STYLE_FIT flag mean it is marginally more vulnerable if its lead role is disrupted.
runners_data.comment: Caprelo has been in the frame in three of his last five starts, including a win, and is already proven at today's trip and going. First-time blinkers add interest, and a leading rating makes him hard to beat, with the 47-day gap the only concern.

runners_data.name: Baileys Khelstar
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for in-form Charlie Johnston stable; course-placed at 16f on Standard and won most recently at 16f on Good, making this trip and surface a plausible fit — sits near the sharp end in the expected race shape, which suits his record of finishing in the first two.
runners_data.comment: Baileys Khelstar won last time out and was runner-up three times in his last six starts, already proven at today's trip and going. A brisk 15-day turnaround has him fresh and dangerous, with a fourth and an unplaced effort among that sequence the only blemishes.

runners_data.name: Barenboim
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's eight-year-old wears a hood and prefers to come from off the pace; recent form figures of 9-8-9 in similar conditions are a concern, though his single placed effort at 16f on Standard suggests he retains ability — needs the pace to be genuinely honest to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Barenboim won and was runner-up earlier in this sequence, and already knows today's trip and going. First-time cheekpieces could freshen him up, but his last four starts have all been well beaten, the clear concern on a 25-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Nunc Est Bibendum
runners_data.note: Three wins from four at 16f on Standard for Gary & Moore, giving this prominent traveller strong credentials on this exact surface and trip combination; 71 days off the track is a minor flag, but the trainer has a win from 28 runners over 14 days and the form record at this track is hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Nunc Est Bibendum landed three wins in this five-race sequence and was runner-up last time, with today's trip and going both proven. Working against her are a 71-day absence and a yard managing just a 4% strike-rate over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Dust Cover
runners_data.note: Won twice at 11f on Standard and has strong recent form, but is a natural prominent-type racer who the race map pushes into midfield due to supply outstripping demand at the front — Ross Burdon's four-year-old will be competing from a position that does not reflect its true style, which tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Dust Cover won twice earlier in this sequence but has since cooled, with a modest fifth his latest effort. He's proven over today's going, though the trip is unproven for him, and a modest speed figure leaves questions after a 54-day absence.

runners_data.name: Gooloogong
runners_data.note: Won at 16f on Standard and has been competitive at this track; Neil Callan keeps it straightforward from a prominent position and the combination of course form and trip suitability makes this a quiet contender if the race is run at a steady-to-fair tempo.
runners_data.comment: Gooloogong has landed two wins in his last five starts and is already proven at today's trip and going. That form makes him a leading threat, though last time's fourth and a modest speed figure leave a little to find.

runners_data.name: Kitty Foyle
runners_data.note: Returns from a 318-day absence (50-day jockey conditional claim) for Daisy Hitchins and Oliver Carmichael; best form has come at considerably longer trips on Good ground, and with zero wins or places on this surface in five attempts, the hold-up style and surface record combine to make it hard to fancy on comeback.
runners_data.comment: Kitty Foyle has been runner-up twice in her last four starts, sandwiched by a fourth and a fifth, though still without a win. She's proven at today's trip and going, and a fair speed figure keeps her competitive, but ending the drought is the obvious question.

runners_data.name: One Cool Dreamer
runners_data.note: Alan King's five-year-old has been off 110 days and carries a peak rating of 69; a genuine prominent-style horse whose natural position is being squeezed out by deeper stayers in this field — Luke Morris will have to decide whether to push forward and use energy early or accept a midfield berth that doesn't suit.
runners_data.comment: One Cool Dreamer has been in the frame with a second and a third in his last five starts, though still without a win in that run. First-time cheekpieces and a fair speed figure offer encouragement, but a 110-day absence and an unproven trip are the concerns.

runners_data.name: Louie's Folly
runners_data.note: Long absence (124 days, 57-day jockey claim) for Denis Hogan's yard and Gina Mangan in the saddle; a hold-up horse with no wins from the back in recent form and no placings on Standard going across five efforts — only enters calculations if the pace genuinely collapses into an attritional test.
runners_data.comment: Louie's Folly is yet to win in her last five starts, with a best of second among modest finishes, and her stable is out of form at 0% over the last fortnight. Today's trip and going are proven, but she sits bottom of this field on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Caprelo is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no horse likely to seriously challenge for the lead in the early stages, should be allowed to dictate at a comfortable, controlled tempo over this 2m Kempton AW trip on Standard to Slow ground. Baileys Khelstar, Nunc Est Bibendum, and Gooloogong are all genuine prominent types and will look to settle just off Caprelo's shoulder, creating a compact early order rather than a strung-out field — but the pace itself is unlikely to be brutal. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions: Dust Cover and One Cool Dreamer are true prominent racers who will find themselves shuffled further back than ideal, with Caprelo and Baileys Khelstar most likely to actually control the race shape from the front. A steady, uncontested gallop on a flat track overwhelmingly favours horses who can sit prominently, travel within themselves, and produce a sustained finishing effort — hold-up horses who need a genuine end-to-end gallop to make ground will be at a structural disadvantage in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Caprelo Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Caprelo bowls along at a comfortable clip and the pace never truly hotly contested, allowing prominent racers to travel into the race.
scenarios.body: Caprelo sets a fair but undemanding tempo, and horses settled just off the pace — notably Baileys Khelstar and Nunc Est Bibendum — have every chance to pounce approaching the final turn and run on strongly; the hold-up horses simply cover too much ground from deep. This shape rewards horses with a clean early position, good Standard to Slow going form, and the ability to sustain their effort over a staying trip rather than produce a sharp sprint.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace drops to a crawl and Caprelo and Baileys Khelstar simply outstay the field in a sprint finish from the front.
scenarios.body: With a genuinely dawdling tempo, the race effectively becomes a two-furlong dash from the home straight and those with the best position — Caprelo and Baileys Khelstar — are perfectly placed to kick clear before any closer can respond. Gooloogong, tracking close throughout, could also emerge as a beneficiary, while true hold-up horses like Barenboim and Kitty Foyle are left with too much to do from the back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves more searching than expected and forces frontrunners to crack in the final quarter-mile, opening the door for patient types.
scenarios.body: Barenboim and Kitty Foyle both sit off the pace and have the stamina for the trip, and a genuinely honest gallop would theoretically bring them into the reckoning late; Louie's Folly could also pick up ground if attrition bites. Note this scenario depends partly on Dust Cover and One Cool Dreamer — natural prominent types who are mapped to midfield and unlikely to be true closers — meaning the genuine hold-up runners here are few and the probability of this shape is suppressed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Cause Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Dust Cover or One Cool Dreamer push forward aggressively from their wide/rear draw, injecting unexpected early pressure and fracturing the expected race shape.
scenarios.body: Racing out of their mapped positions and forced to work harder than ideal early, these horses could unsettle Caprelo's rhythm and turn the race into a more attritional contest than anticipated; however, given their STYLE_FIT discounts, both are likely to pay a price for the effort later. The unsettled shape in this scenario would most benefit a fresh, stamina-rich stayer like Nunc Est Bibendum who has been patient and can capitalise on a scrambled pace.

watchPoints.text: Baileys Khelstar (Oisin Murphy) has won or finished second in four of his last five and sits in the prime seat just off Caprelo — his combination of course form, in-form jockey, and prominent style makes him the central danger in the dominant scenario.

Dust Cover and One Cool Dreamer are both natural front-runners whose handlers may opt to push forward regardless of the race map — any attempt by either to force their way prominent early could disrupt Caprelo's uncontested lead and fundamentally alter the race shape.

Nunc Est Bibendum has three wins at exactly 16f on Standard but is stepped up to 2m for this test — watch whether Lewis Edmunds rides positively, as a prominent position would play to the horse's strengths, but a passive ride risks it getting swallowed up in a compact finish.

Kitty Foyle is returning from a 318-day absence with a conditional jockey claim; on a surface where it has no placed form in five attempts, it represents a significant risk as a hold-up horse that needs both a strong pace and a good comeback run to feature.

Standard to Slow going (confirmed in the going report for this race) adds a stamina premium to this already-searching 2m trip — any horse whose form is built around faster surfaces or shorter distances faces an additional structural test tonight.

races.name: Unibet Supporting Safer Gambling Handicap

runners_data.name: Roi De Coeur
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Marco Botti with Marco Ghiani aboard; placed in 2 of 3 runs on Standard going but yet to win or place on this course, and at 23 days fresh his form profile suggests a mid-to-late challenge that needs the pace to be genuinely strong to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in three runs (5th, 6th, 7th) but he sits clear atop our figures and already knows today's distance. Fit again after a 23-day break, carrying 135lb from stall 5, moderate recent form is the only blot on an otherwise clear leading claim.

runners_data.name: Thestral
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard AW and placed twice in similar conditions for Hugo Palmer; Neil Callan's experience at Kempton is a plus, and 1W2P from 6 similar-going starts suggests this horse handles the surface well — a hold-up ride that needs a true pace, which this race may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Boasts a win in his last five starts and has rounded into form with back-to-back places (2nd, 3rd) after a blip. Proven over today's distance and going and fit again after 23 days, he ranks 2nd on our figures from 135lb — the main risk is a repeat of that one flat run.

runners_data.name: Tales Old As Time
runners_data.note: Long absence of 258 days is a significant concern, and the flagged tendency to fade in the finish compounds that worry; placed once from 3 similar-going starts but the freshness and weak finishing profile make this a difficult proposition on return.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten last time after a promising 3rd two runs back, and it's now 258 days since he was last seen — a big question over fitness. Winless in his last three starts, though proven over today's distance and going, he ranks only 7th of 14 on our figures from 133lb.

runners_data.name: Thisonesforyou
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner with a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93, indicating she is racing outside her most comfortable role as a prominent-racing type stepping up to lead; her lone win came over 8f on Good, and Clive Cox sends her here fresh enough at 25 days — the key factor is whether she can translate that tactical freedom into a controlled performance.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back but has since faded — a fifth and then last time's ninth leave the form book mixed. Proven over today's distance and fit again after 25 days, he sits mid-pack on our figures from 133lb — the recent decline is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Music Academy
runners_data.note: Visored hold-up type for Ralph Beckett with Rossa Ryan, who has form on both Standard and Soft; 0W1P from 4 similar-going runs and no win since debut suggests this horse needs things to fall right, and being squeezed out of a natural hold-up berth by the crowded rear of the field is a structural disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a modest split of finishes — a 3rd sandwiched between two off-form efforts — and no clear upward trend. Fit again 30 days after her latest run and proven over today's distance and going, she's rated only 10th of 14 from 133lb.

runners_data.name: Katalyst
runners_data.note: Blinkers applied and a hold-up profile that has found horses finishing 4th-to-10th in five recent outings on similar ground; William Muir & Chris Grassick send him here at 35 days, but 0W0P on Standard going and the fact the field's overcrowded rear will push him forward of his preferred spot creates a compounding problem.
runners_data.comment: A modest sort who has never threatened to win in her last five starts and was even further back last time out. Blinkers go on for the first time in search of an edge, but from 132lb and rated only 11th of 14, she has plenty to find on these figures.

runners_data.name: Roccobear
runners_data.note: Seven runs at 7f on Standard going for J R Jenkins with 0W2P tells a consistent but limited story; Jack Callan's 3lb claim provides some relief, though the horse's hold-up style will be disrupted by the crowded field configuration that forces him into a closer position than he would naturally choose.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but rarely far away, with a 2nd among those efforts and a workmanlike 3rd last time. Fit again after a 57-day break and already proven over today's distance and going, he's third in our figures from 132lb — the layoff is the only real question.

runners_data.name: Sports Day
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes over for Michael Bell on a horse whose best recent run was 3rd over 10f on Good — the step down to 1m on Standard is not obviously ideal; a genuine hold-up performer who has only one comparable Standard outing, and the redistribution into midfield means he will not find his natural rhythm easily.
runners_data.comment: Winless in five starts and outside the frame last time after a promising spell of 2nd and 3rd two and three runs back. Fit again 23 days on and proven over today's distance and going, he sits mid-table on our figures from 132lb, with more to prove after that recent dip.

runners_data.name: Torbados
runners_data.note: Blinkers on for Charles Hills and Jason Watson, with a mixed profile over 6-7f on Standard and Good; 43 days since last run and only 2 places from 8 similar-going starts makes this a horse needing significant improvement, and the race shape does not obviously set him up to deliver it.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but with a solid 3rd in that sequence and respectable figures throughout, he's fourth-rated in this field from 131lb. First-time blinkers could sharpen him up after a 43-day break, and he's already proven over today's distance and going — the danger if they work.

runners_data.name: Ten Cuidado
runners_data.note: A two-year-old form horse returning after 189 days for Mark Usher; 4 runs entirely at shorter trips (5-7f) with the longest being 7f makes the step to 1m a question mark, and the lengthy absence alongside the style redistribution leaves Tyler Heard with a complex tactical brief.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our figures here and out of the frame last time, with 189 days since his latest run adding a big fitness question. Winless in his last four starts, though he does go over a distance he's raced before, carrying 130lb from stall 4 — this looks a tough spot.

runners_data.name: Positive Thoughts
runners_data.note: Only genuine prominent runner aside from the leader, making Oisin Murphy's positioning straightforward; 0W1P from 6 similar-going starts is modest, but the tactical advantage of being able to naturally slot into second or third off a slow pace is the clearest structural edge in this field outside the leader herself.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but with a solid 2nd in there and a fair spread of form since, she's fifth-rated in this field from 130lb. First-time cheekpieces are added after a 30-day break, and she has raced over today's distance before — the erratic finishes are the only worry.

runners_data.name: Blue Celestial
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form — 5 placings from 9 similar-going runs — for James Tate with Saffie Osborne; ran just 10 days ago over 10f on Standard, so fitness is assured, and the hold-up style suits a patient ride, though being mapped to midfield means she will need to thread through traffic rather than produce a clean late run.
runners_data.comment: A model of consistency — in the first four in five of her last six starts (3rd last time) — but still winless throughout. Backed up quickly after just 10 days, proven over today's distance and going, and from a yard in good recent form, she's ninth on our figures from 129lb.

runners_data.name: Betty Lemon
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good for Hughie Morrison and returns just 15 days after her last run in good nick; a hold-up type pushed into a midfield map position by the field's composition, though the recent win shows she is capable — Rose Dawes' 5lb claim is a minor assist on a competitive mark of 57.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to end a moderate run of finishes and returns quickly after just 15 days. Proven over today's distance and going, she's rated only 12th of 14 from 127lb, so this looks a stiffer task against a deeper field.

runners_data.name: Fallacious Promise
runners_data.note: Most active horse in the field, running just 2 days ago, with a sharp recent form profile of 1-2-2-3 suggesting John Butler has her in a rich vein; a genuine hold-up performer by style, mapped closer than ideal by the crowded rear, but the current form wave and Luke Morris's tactical awareness make her one of the more interesting cases despite the redistribution note.
runners_data.comment: Winless in five starts despite a pair of seconds in the middle of that sequence, and his figures have since tailed off to a modest 3rd last time. Fit again after 34 days and proven over today's distance and going, he's second-from-bottom on our figures from 129lb.

races.paceDynamic: Thisonesforyou is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to challenge for the lead, Georgia Dobie should be able to dictate a measured, controlled gallop from the front on what is Standard To Slow ground at Kempton's Polytrack mile. Positive Thoughts is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely slot in second or third, meaning the early pace is unlikely to be pressured — a sustainable, single-file tempo is the most probable race shape. With the pace so compressed at the front, the field of predominantly hold-up types will bunch behind, setting up a test of finishing quality rather than stamina, which on a flat all-weather mile typically rewards horses who can travel smoothly into contention rather than those forced to come from far back. The redistribution flag is significant here: Sports Day, Roccobear, Katalyst, Torbados, Ten Cuidado, Blue Celestial, Betty Lemon, and Fallacious Promise are all genuine hold-up horses who cannot all find space at the rear and will be pushed closer than their natural position — those best equipped to race prominently or in mid-division off a slow tempo, travelling within themselves, hold the clearest structural advantage, making the race shape most favourable for prominent or mid-division types who can quicken from a handy position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Thisonesforyou leads unchallenged and controls the tempo throughout, covering the field at will.
scenarios.body: Thisonesforyou sets a comfortable, measured pace and the slow-burn gallop on Standard To Slow ground allows her to conserve energy before the home straight; with no rival able to apply genuine pressure, she could simply lengthen and hold on up the Polytrack straight. Positive Thoughts, tracking closely in second, is the primary beneficiary if the leader tires, as the prominent profile suits a race run at this controlled tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Finishers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly slow and the field compresses, allowing mid-division runners to cruise into contention and finish strongly.
scenarios.body: A crawling tempo collapses the field into a tight group, negating any disadvantage for runners sitting fourth to eighth; those with the sharpest turn of foot can peel off the rail and deliver their challenge without needing to cover ground. Blue Celestial's consistent placed form on this surface and distance, and Fallacious Promise's recent sharp finishing, make them the prime candidates to sweep through a compressed field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than expected and the field strings out, allowing a genuine closer to produce a late burst from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Should Positive Thoughts push Thisonesforyou into a faster-than-anticipated gallop, the race could open up for a true hold-up performer to finish through horses in the final two furlongs; on Standard To Slow ground, the premium on stamina rises and late runners gain ground. Thestral, who won at this course and distance on Standard, and Roi De Coeur both carry hold-up profiles and the form to capitalise if they can find a clear run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Leader Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Thisonesforyou overcooks the pace or the slow ground saps her stamina, leaving the prominent-to-mid pack to battle it out.
scenarios.body: A leader who has gone too soon on tiring ground would see the finish line reached in a scrappy, extended drive with the prize going to whoever has been most economical with their energy mid-race; this scenario slightly re-energises horses like Music Academy or Sports Day who have been pushed off their natural hold-up berth but travel well. Neither has dominant form credentials, but the tactical scramble could bring them into play at bigger prices.

watchPoints.text: Thisonesforyou sets a slow, uncontested lead — watch whether Georgia Dobie elects to quicken sharply entering the final 2f to catch the field flat-footed, as a controlled front-runner on slow ground is historically very hard to peg back at Kempton.

Fallacious Promise ran just two days ago and John Butler has her in explosive form (1-2-2-3); watch for Luke Morris positioning her closer than the hold-up redistribution suggests, as a fresh-legged horse in form is a live threat regardless of the structural map.

Blue Celestial ran 10 days ago over 10f and drops back to 1m — watch how Saffie Osborne manages the early pace, as this filly has placed six times on similar ground and could be quietly set up for a strong finish if she gets a clean passage through the midfield.

Positive Thoughts with Oisin Murphy is the only natural companion for Thisonesforyou at the head of affairs — watch whether Murphy allows a gap to open to the leader or sits tight, as that tactical decision will shape whether the pace quickens early or stays truly slow into the straight.

The going report confirms Standard To Slow for this 7:48 slot — watch for horses who have previously posted good figures on Standard but whose form tails off on slower variants, as several runners in this field have form strings heavily biased toward Standard rather than Slow ground.

races.name: Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Handicap (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Volto Di Medusa
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with a solid sim-going strike rate on comparable surfaces (2W from 10 runs), but form figures of 5-0-7-9-1-0 are inconsistent; the uncontested pace here may leave him with too little to close into and the 22-day break with headgear (p) flagged is not a standout angle.
runners_data.comment: Volto Di Medusa won two starts back but was unplaced last time out, a boom-or-bust profile that includes a spread of finishes in between. He is already proven at today's trip and going, and first-time cheekpieces could bring more consistency, though the inconsistency itself is the main knock against him.

runners_data.name: Platinum Prince
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: a confirmed front-runner landing on a flat, galloping track where he can control the tempo entirely alone; sim-going figures on this surface are poor (0W0P from 2 runs) and trainer Gary & Josh Moore are in decent 14-day form (2/24), but the racing-out-of-role STYLE_FIT flag is irrelevant here — this is very much his natural position.
runners_data.comment: Platinum Prince won and was runner-up either side of that success earlier in this sequence, before form dipped over his last three starts. He already goes well at today's trip and going, and first-time blinkers offer an obvious source of renewed sharpness, with the recent decline the clear concern.

runners_data.name: Thapa VC
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the mount on this hold-up type whose best recent form is over 7-8f in good ground; sim-going record is modest (0W0P from 6 comparable runs), and while the 25-day break is fine, he needs a stronger pace than Platinum Prince is likely to set to deliver his finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Thapa Vc has been consistently in the frame, with a second and a run of thirds in this six-start sequence, and that steady profile, still without a win, leads these ratings. First-time tongue-tie and blinkers add real scope for improvement from stall eleven.

runners_data.name: Six Blue
runners_data.note: Stepping back down from extreme distances (16f) to a mile, with a form string showing consistent mid-pack finishes; sim-going record is 0W0P from 3 runs and the 58-day absence is a mild concern — hold-up style here makes him reliant on a pace scenario the race shape is unlikely to produce.
runners_data.comment: Six Blue remains without a win, having finished fifth, fifth and sixth in a short recent sequence, though the exposure is limited. She is proven over today's going, and a competitive speed figure keeps her in this puzzle, with the unproven trip and a 58-day gap the main queries.

runners_data.name: Gladiadora
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins and three places from six similar-going runs — ideally placed for this race shape; Charlie Clover's yard had one winner in the last six days, Saffie Osborne takes over, and recent form (1-2-4 in last three STA/GOO runs) reads well for tracking a slow leader into the straight.
runners_data.comment: Gladiadora has been a fairly consistent frame-filler, with a win and a second earlier in this six-race sequence followed by a run of fourths, including last time. She already has today's distance in the book, but a modest speed figure caps her upside.

runners_data.name: Relevant Range
runners_data.note: Experienced prominent racer who handles Standard (2W6P from 9 comparable runs) and is drawn to sit just off Platinum Prince; Elle-May Croot (5) claims 5lb which matters in a 0-65, though the trainer's 14-day record (1/32) is lean and a recent sixth from eight runners tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Relevant Range was a clear second last time out, his best effort in a mixed six-start sequence that remains without a win. He already has today's distance in the book on a sharp 16-day turnaround, though the yard is out of form at just 3% over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Mbappe
runners_data.note: Jack Callan (3) rides this horse who is a natural hold-up performer but is shown in midfield here because the field's composition pushes true closers forward on the map; one win from 11 runs on this surface and a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 signal he is running partially out of his preferred position — needs more pace injection than likely.
runners_data.comment: Mbappe won three starts back but has since cooled with a sixth and seventh in his last two starts. He is already proven at today's trip and going, and first-time cheekpieces plus a brisk 13-day turnaround offer some hope of a bounce, though the modest speed figure is a concern.

runners_data.name: Chico Dulce
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with an outstanding sim-going record (2W4P from 13 comparable runs at Kempton AW), returning from a 79-day break which is the primary concern; trainer Madgwick has had no runners in the last two weeks and no market support data, but the surface profile makes him interesting if fit.
runners_data.comment: Chico Dulce won earlier in this five-race sequence but has since faded to a run of modest finishes, including a seventh last time out. He is already proven at today's trip and going, and a fair speed figure hints at ability, though a 79-day absence is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Luminous Approach
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse shown in midfield on the map due to the surplus of closers in this field; David Probert's experience helps, but four runs yielding 0W0P on sim-going, a 60-day absence and a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 mean conditions are stacked against him.
runners_data.comment: Luminous Approach remains without a win in his last four starts, none of them threatening the frame, though he is already proven at today's trip and going. A fair speed figure offers a little encouragement, but a 60-day absence and a modest form line make him hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Lovely Jubly
runners_data.note: Carries a finish-fade flag and a 210-day absence — the longest layoff in the field — which is a significant concern irrespective of anything else; Gina Mangan rides, and while a previous win at 8f/HEA shows ability, this hold-up style mapped to midfield and the layoff make this a difficult profile to support.
runners_data.comment: Lovely Jubly won three starts back, following two unplaced efforts, but the form has since cooled with a sixth and last time's eighth, and she now returns from a lengthy 210-day absence. She is proven at today's trip and going, but the long gap and recent decline leave plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Summer Evening
runners_data.note: Returning after 20 days with headgear (htb) flagged, this four-year-old hold-up type has 0W2P from 11 comparable runs and a career-worst of 21st on soft ground; mapped to midfield due to the redistribution of closers, Tyler Heard faces a tough task generating enough momentum from a slow pace to make a meaningful impact.
runners_data.comment: Summer Evening remains without a win in her last six starts, and the trend points the wrong way with a ninth last time out after modest form before that. She already has today's distance in the book, but she sits bottom of this field on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Platinum Prince is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate terms at whatever tempo suits him on a Standard To Slow Kempton surface. That controlled, uncontested gallop is most likely to produce a steadily-run race where the early pace is modest and the race pivots in the final two furlongs. Prominent riders Gladiadora and Relevant Range will sit close behind Platinum Prince and are best placed to capitalise on a tactical shape, while the cluster of hold-up types — Mbappe, Luminous Approach, Lovely Jubly and Summer Evening — are all true closers squeezed into midfield because the field contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear, meaning those genuinely held-up animals will likely find less ground to make up than usual and are running partially out of their natural style. This race shape firmly favours prominent racers who can track a slow-moderate pace, hit the front entering the straight, and sustain a run — hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to close into are structurally disadvantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Platinum Prince Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Platinum Prince dictates a comfortable, uncontested tempo and the race develops as a procession until the straight.
scenarios.body: Platinum Prince rolls along in front without pressure, slowing the pace to a crawl before quickening in the straight, and horses who track him closely benefit most from the decisive final-furlong sprint.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Sprint Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the race is slow-paced early and the prominent brigade quicken from two out in a cluster finish.
scenarios.body: A modest gallop compresses the field into a bunch by halfway, setting up a sprint-finish where prominent horses who haven't been exposed to early pressure hold the energy advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is marginally stronger than expected and enough daylight opens for genuine closers to weave through.
scenarios.body: Even a slightly stronger tempo off the front would suit the redistributed hold-up horses — particularly Mbappe and Volto Di Medusa — who find room to power through in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Platinum Prince Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If no one challenges his lead at any stage and Platinum Prince simply outstays all comers from the front.
scenarios.body: Having been untroublbled throughout, Platinum Prince uses his front-running experience to repel challengers in the straight on a surface he handles adequately.

watchPoints.text: Platinum Prince's ability to dictate the exact tempo unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaper — if he crawls, the entire field compresses into a sprint finish that eliminates genuine hold-up horses entirely.

Gladiadora and Relevant Range will fight for the same prominent position just behind Platinum Prince — if they crowd each other early in a slowly-run race, neither may get the clean run they need entering the straight.
Chico Dulce's 79-day absence is the key unknown for a horse with the best Kempton AW sim-going profile in the field — watch the market move to gauge fitness confidence from the Madgwick yard.

Mbappe, Luminous Approach, Lovely Jubly and Summer Evening are all true hold-up horses running partially out of their natural style due to the field composition — if the pace unexpectedly quickens from halfway, one of this group could emerge, but the race shape makes it structurally unlikely.

Lovely Jubly's 210-day layoff combined with a documented finish-fade tendency makes her an extreme watch for early signs of rustiness in the parade ring — any market drift should be noted given the layoff concern.

races.name: Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Handicap (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Spirit Lead Me
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Richard Hughes who has form on this surface (sim-going 8/15) but carries a recurring fade-in-finish flag that is a genuine worry when the sprint is sharp; Donagh Murphy's 7lb claim helps the weight but does not disguise the finishing concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts and rarely troubling the frame, with three separate 9th-placed efforts in that run. First-time cheekpieces offer some hope of a change after a 24-day break, and he does go over a distance and going he's raced before, but he's rated only 8th of 11 here from 135lb.

runners_data.name: Union Island
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's yard in respectable form (T14: 5/48) and this five-year-old has a winning run over 8f on Good ground; hold-up style suits a slow-pace sprint, and Jack Callan's 3lb claim gives a slight weight edge over many rivals.
runners_data.comment: Won five runs back and has stayed competitive since — a fifth then a fourth, third and fourth in turn. Quick to back up after just 16 days, proven over today's distance and going, and fitted with first-time cheekpieces, he sits mid-pack on our figures from 134lb.

runners_data.name: Look Back Smiling
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Neil Mulholland and brings top-draw jockey craft to a horse whose sim-going record is thin (2/15); 33 days off may have freshened this six-year-old, though it has not placed on comparable AW going and the form string contains a wide miss.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but he boasts by far the strongest figures in this field on speed. First-time cheekpieces go on after a 33-day break, and he's already proven over today's distance and going — his moderate recent finishes are the only concern on an otherwise clear leading claim.

runners_data.name: Opening Bat
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's four-year-old is a genuine rear-of-field type forced further up the map than it naturally races; recent form shows back-to-back nil positions (00) and it failed to fire on Good ground last time, though it has sim-going placed runs (3/7f/STA, 3/8f/GOO) worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and his last two efforts brought no finish in the frame, a step back after a pair of 3rds before that. Fit again after 24 days and proven over today's distance and going, he's third-rated here from 132lb — the recent dip is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Finn Ironside
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's five-year-old holds its best form at 7f and the step to a mile is a query; Elle-May Croot's 5lb claim is useful but the horse's true deep hold-up style means it will need everything to fall right in a sprint finish, and its sim-going record at the trip is modest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts but with a promising 3rd in the middle of that run, form since has tailed off to 8th and 7th. First-time tongue-tie could help sharpen him after a quick 16-day turnaround, and he's proven over today's distance and going, though his stable is out of form, which adds a query.

runners_data.name: Between Me And U
runners_data.note: David Probert is a strong booking for Michael Herrington's yard (T14: 4/18) and this horse has a placed run over 8f on soft and standard surfaces; it is a natural hold-up type that will sit deep and look for daylight, and the headgear flag (hg:t) suggests it needs to be switched on.
runners_data.comment: Winless in five starts, but a 2nd and 3rd earlier in that run show he's not without ability, even though his last two efforts (6th, 7th) have tailed off. First-time tongue-tie follows a 23-day break, and he's already proven over today's distance and going — second on our figures from 130lb.

runners_data.name: Devious Devan
runners_data.note: Muir & Grassick's five-year-old carries a win over 8f on Standard going (1/8f/STA) buried in its history and is the most interesting runner if anyone decides to press on early; 34 days fresh, no headgear, and a trainer currently quiet (T14: 0/16) tempers enthusiasm but the form line holds a bounce.
runners_data.comment: Won two runs back but could only finish 7th last time out, leaving mixed form to work with. Fit again after 34 days and proven over today's distance and going, he carries useful speed figures for this grade from 128lb, sitting mid-pack on our overall figures.

runners_data.name: Sub Thirteen
runners_data.note: Jeremy Scott's runner is habitually a deep hold-up type, with its best form sprinting at 6f rather than the mile trip asked here; the sim-going record is modest (0W1P) and the trainer is largely inactive over the last fortnight, though Georgia Dobie's 5lb claim keeps it competitive on weight.
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts and yet to build on a promising 2nd three runs back, with a blank and an 8th following that effort. First-time cheekpieces are tried after a 23-day break, and he has raced over today's distance and going before, but he's only ninth-rated here from 124lb.

runners_data.name: Beau Jardine
runners_data.note: Rachel Cook & John Bridger's eight-year-old landed a win last time out (1/7f/SOF) and brings some momentum into this; hold-up by nature and placed at pace on slower surfaces (hg:p), Luke Morris gives this veteran experience in a tactical race though the step up to 8f from 7f trips is untested recently.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to cap a steadily improving run of finishes — 7th, 7th, 6th, 4th, then a win. Backs up here after 32 days off, proven over today's distance and going, and fitted with first-time cheekpieces, he's seventh on our figures from a light 122lb.

runners_data.name: Hawaiian King
runners_data.note: Michael Madgwick's four-year-old has been campaigned at 10-12f and drops back to a mile here, which is speculative; sim-going record is moderate (0W1P at STA), trainer very quiet (T14: 0/1), and Gina Mangan faces a tough ask — but if the slow pace suits an unexpectedly forward move, a bold price is attached.
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts and never better than 4th in that sequence, with recent finishes trending in the wrong direction. Fit again 20 days on and proven over today's distance and going, he's second-from-bottom on our figures from just 116lb, making a repeat of past efforts unlikely to be good enough.

runners_data.name: Cherry Hill
runners_data.note: Dominic Ffrench Davis's five-year-old has a deeply uninspiring form string (00-800) with double-digit finishes in most recent starts on Standard going; the horse has no win or place at sim going across 15 runs and Tyler Heard faces an uphill battle to find competitive form here at any price.
runners_data.comment: Well held in each of her last five starts, with an 8th her best effort in that run, and she anchors our figures for this race from just 116lb. Fit again after 36 days and proven over today's distance and going, she has a great deal to find on this evidence.

races.paceDynamic: This is an unusual race in that every declared runner carries a hold-up profile, meaning there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse with a natural inclination to stride on from the gates. With Standard To Slow going officially confirmed for the 8:55 slot at Kempton, the pace is likely to be dawdling through the early stages as everyone waits for someone else to set sail, before the field compresses into a late sprint finish from the home turn. The absence of genuine pace means the race will almost certainly be run at an uneven tempo — crawl early, sprint late — over Kempton's flat, turning mile. That dynamic categorically suits hold-up horses who can produce a sharp finishing burst from a pocket, though the irony here is that every runner fits that description, making draw, positioning luck, and jockey awareness of the tactical void the decisive factors. With every runner in the field holding hold-up credentials, the horse best placed to read the slow pace, avoid being caught flat-footed, and produce the cleanest run through will have the clearest advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is predictably slow and the race detonates into a wall-to-wall sprint from the home turn.
scenarios.body: The field drifts along at a crawl before a mass sprint develops, rewarding the horse with the sharpest turn of foot and clearest passage from the turn in; hold-up horses with good recent finishing figures on similar AW surfaces benefit most here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos Suits Alert Mover
scenarios.trigger: If one horse or a small group decides to press on mid-race to exploit the vacuum, triggering a different pace shape.
scenarios.body: A horse that reads the tactical situation and pushes forward from the midfield in the back straight effectively gets a lead and outstays rivals who are slow to respond; a horse with any prominent-race experience hidden in its history gains an edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Draw And Luck Rule The Day
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that a logjam develops on the turn, making clean passage entirely dependent on stall position and jockey awareness.
scenarios.body: Horses drawn widest will have the clearest daylight into the straight while those on the inner get squeezed in traffic; late finishers with strong recent AW form and an experienced jockey navigating the bunching benefit most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Defies The Shape
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpectedly bold move from a low-rated runner creates a pace distortion that flatters an underdog landing a blow.
scenarios.body: A runner who finds daylight early and steals a march while rivals are still waiting on each other can sneak clear in a race where no one is naturally watching the front; lower-rated horses with sharp finishing records on AW can spring a surprise.

watchPoints.text: With no confirmed pace-setter, watch for the moment the field exits the back straight — if no horse has pressed on by halfway, the entire field will sprint from 2f out and position at the turn becomes decisive; horses on the wide outside draw will have the clearest run.

Union Island and Spirit Lead Me both carry hold-up profiles and are backed by strong jockey bookings — if they both track the same split of the field into the home turn, a pocket-racing scenario becomes likely and one of them may find no room at the critical moment.

Beau Jardine is dropping back from 7f to 8f on AW after winning last time; a fresh horse coming off a win can be keen in a slowly-run race and may travel better than its natural hold-up style suggests — watch it in the early exchanges.

Devious Devan's single Standard-going win over 8f (1/8f/STA) stands out in a field of modest form on the surface — if the slow pace scenario favours the horse with any prior experience of winning in these conditions, that run is worth marking.

Cherry Hill has finished outside the top eight in all five recent starts on Standard-going and represents the bottom of the market with good reason; any notable market move for this runner before post time warrants attention given how weak its overall profile looks on paper.
